notes.subject: car
notes.text: The whole car is blurred, but a front-right antenna shows, noticeably closer to the camera than on the nearby Guam car.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Wooden poles, often with a crossbar at the top; the nearby Guam mostly has concrete ones.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Street signs are blue, whereas Guam uses green ones.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Tropical climate with dense, fairly low vegetation.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: The royal poinciana, the official tree, is very common: a wide crown with bright red flowers. It is not common on Guam.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Roads often carry a very large number of road reflectors, as in Guam.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Signs in Japanese, Chinese, Korean and even Russian are common, as also in Guam.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: Only the main island has car coverage; islands to the north have none, and the ones to the south have tripod coverage only.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Dense commercial areas lie on the southern half of the west coast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A steep cliff with lots of exposed rock near the northern tip of the main island.
